headline: Court cancels Pori Moni's bail, issues arrest warrant
summary: The actress is set to surrender before the court tomorrow after failing to appear for witness testimony due to illness.
details: A Dhaka court has cancelled the bail of film actress Pori Moni and issued a warrant for her arrest. The order was passed by Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Mahfuzur Rahman.
The legal action follows a case filed in 2022 by former Uttara Club Limited president Nasir U Mahmud, who alleged assault, vandalism, attempted murder, and intimidation.
The court's decision came after the prosecution filed a petition to cancel her bail. Pori Moni failed to appear for scheduled witness testimony today, citing an allergy-related illness.
Earlier, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted a charge sheet against Pori Moni and her costume designer, Junaid Karim Jimmy, in March 2024.
The court had framed charges against the actress and Jimmy on January 26, 2025. Another individual, Fatema-tuz-Jannat Bony, was discharged from the case.
In a separate legal battle, Pori Moni had filed a case against Nasir U Mahmud and two others in June 2021, alleging attempted rape and murder.
caption:
Actress Pori Moni's bail has been cancelled and an arrest warrant issued. She is expected to surrender tomorrow.

A Dhaka court has cancelled the bail of film actress Pori Moni and issued a warrant for her arrest. The order was passed by Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Mahfuzur Rahman.

The legal action follows a case filed in 2022 by former Uttara Club Limited president Nasir U Mahmud, who alleged assault, vandalism, attempted murder, and intimidation.

The court's decision came after the prosecution filed a petition to cancel her bail. Pori Moni failed to appear for scheduled witness testimony today, citing an allergy-related illness.

Earlier, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted a charge sheet against Pori Moni and her costume designer, Junaid Karim Jimmy, in March 2024.

The court had framed charges against the actress and Jimmy on January 26, 2025. Another individual, Fatema-tuz-Jannat Bony, was discharged from the case.

In a separate legal battle, Pori Moni had filed a case against Nasir U Mahmud and two others in June 2021, alleging attempted rape and murder.

headline_marked: 100+ garment factories [[shut amid protests and clashes]] in Savar, Ashulia
headline: 100+ garment factories shut amid protests and clashes in Savar, Ashulia
summary: Workers demand a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, leading to road blockades and violent confrontations with police.
details: More than 100 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared holidays today as workers protested for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
Thousands of workers walked out and blocked roads in several areas, including Ulail, Fulbaria, Ghoshbagh, and Hemayetpur, leading to violent clashes with police.
Around 30,000 to 40,000 workers gathered near Padmar Mor, where they attacked police and set fire to a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station.
The officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station was seriously injured in the attack, and police used sound grenades and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
Several journalists were also injured during the reports, including Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, who was assaulted while broadcasting live.
Police have detained over 30 people, including one person found with a crude bomb, and are investigating whether third-party groups are manipulating the unrest to destabilize the country.
caption:
Over 100 garment factories shut down as thousands of workers clash with police over wage demands.

More than 100 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared holidays today as workers protested for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

Thousands of workers walked out and blocked roads in several areas, including Ulail, Fulbaria, Ghoshbagh, and Hemayetpur, leading to violent clashes with police.

Around 30,000 to 40,000 workers gathered near Padmar Mor, where they attacked police and set fire to a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station.

The officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station was seriously injured in the attack, and police used sound grenades and tear gas to disperse the crowds.

Several journalists were also injured during the reports, including Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, who was assaulted while broadcasting live.

Police have detained over 30 people, including one person found with a crude bomb, and are investigating whether third-party groups are manipulating the unrest to destabilize the country.
